style: Use case: illustration-story. One standalone full-bleed landscape 3:2 illustration for an original Japanese children's SF picture book. Nostalgic 1965-1975 Showa-era printed children's science-fiction picture book, hand-painted gouache and colored pencil, delicate dark ink, visible paper grain, slightly imperfect lithographic ink, ultramarine night blue, vermilion and warm golden yellow, cinematic tenderness and cosmic wonder. NOT modern anime, NOT chibi, NOT 3D. Absolutely no typography, letters, numbers, captions, borders, logos. Consistent main character Mio: six-year-old Japanese girl, short straight black bob, one small red hairclip on left, mustard-yellow long-sleeved tunic, dark navy overalls, red flat shoes, normal child proportions, dot-like dark eyes. Father: slim Japanese man, short untidy black hair, round glasses, teal cardigan, cream shirt. Alien: very tall gentle rust-red humanoid with two small black curved horns, folded dark plum bat wings, long pointed tail, simple cream cape, kind solemn face, NOT scary.
scenes: At dusk in a modest 1960s Japanese town with tiled roofs, power poles and a tiny bakery, an immense smooth silver saucer hangs perfectly still above the town. Mio in foreground holds father's hand; seen from behind looking up. Stars just appearing, orange horizon. Enormous scale yet comforting stillness.

Inside a warmly lit retro Japanese living room with a wooden CRT television, tatami and low table, Mio solemnly offers one red paper origami flower to the very tall winged horned alien, who kneels courteously to fit below ceiling. Father with glasses peeks around doorway in surprise. Silver saucer visible through window. Delightful incongruity, humane not slapstick.

Mio and three different fully clothed young children (boy in striped blue shirt, girl with braids in green sweater, boy with curly hair in red jacket) are peacefully asleep in a circle on a deep blue field of dreams. Thin threads of starlight gently connect above their heads into a huge complex spiral galaxy; a modest house and Earth sit at bottom. Wonder, psychic connection, no transparent bodies.

Inside immense round silver spaceship observatory, Mio stands beside the gentle red alien and looks up at a great luminous galaxy whose many tiny stars are streaming together toward a single immense white glow. Small analog scientific control dials in foreground. The child holds a small folded cream paper letter firmly in her hands. Awe with slight melancholy.

Close tender scene: Mio and father sit on tatami facing each other at a low table, a blank cream paper letter and pencil between them, father's large hand beside her small hand. He listens carefully with wet shining eyes, she is earnest, no tears pouring, quiet affection. The alien silhouette waits respectfully outside open sliding door, night stars.

Cosmic turning point. Mio stands safely on a silver observation deck and holds open a tiny folded cream paper letter toward a vast spiral galaxy. Its stars form many separate individual warm points linked by fine luminous winding threads, retaining dark spaces between them, NOT one merged white mass. The very tall red horned alien watches in gentle astonishment. Big scale; hopeful, handcrafted retro SF.

A modest Japanese town in bright clear morning after a cosmic event. Mio and children outdoors beneath a departing enormous silver saucer, exchanging blank postcards by a bright red old-fashioned cylindrical postbox. A bicycle, potted morning glories and a sleepy cat. Alien at spaceship ramp holding a tiny paper origami flower. Lightness, everyday life transformed.

Quiet final scene years later: father slightly older with a few gray hairs and round glasses stands at open wooden doorway on a golden morning; Mio now age twelve, recognizably same bob and red hairclip, mustard jacket, navy trousers, red shoes, small navy backpack, walks away toward a small silver rocket at the end of the garden, turns back and waves. Father holds a very small old pair of red child's shoes. Dawn sky filled with faint stars. No sadness melodrama, warm brave farewell, spacious composition.
